Bhaiya's Teachings — Knowledge Base (Session 46, English)
Bhaiya's Guru Journey: The Night of Vision, the Origin of "Jai Siyaram," and the Dimension of Past-Life Tapasya

Sour ce: a live Ashaeiynn Mool T atva satsang opening with a discussion of the sangat's rapidly accelerating drishti-openings and the ongoing demand for mantra-jaap/aura checking, befor e a sangat member's dir ect question pr ompts Bhaiya to narrate, in far gr eater personal detail than in prior sessions, the full story of his own first vision of Hanuman Ji Maharaj, the specific origin of his "Jai Siyaram" mantra, his five years of struggle befor e his own drishti opened, and the "dimension" concept explaining why that struggle took so long.
1. Extraordinary Gr owth in Drishti-Openings

1. Bhaiya opens by stating that the collective decision to perform jaap on behalf of the sangat is bearing fruit at an unprecedented, unlimited level — devotees ar e receiving darshan in rapid succession, with a new video documenting this released that same day , and weekly video updates to continue tracking this ongoing pattern.
2. Why the Constant Demand for Mantra/Aura Checking Is Actually Justified

1. Bhaiya acknowledges that the sangat r equests checking far mor e than his mentors would pr efer — mentors have jokingly complained that "their sinful stomachs ar e never satisfied" — but he states he agr ees the underlying impulse is legitimate. 2. His explanation: in the physical world, effort does not visibly show its r esults to the person making that effort — everyone in the sangat has been sufficiently "knocked ar ound" by life to know firsthand that physical-world effort doesn't r eliably pay off — so people naturally seek r eassurance in the subtle world (the world of Ram) instead, wanting to know that negativity is being clear ed and Ram's energy is arriving in its place. 3. This teaching states this underlying anxiety and desir e for checking is completely understandable — a genuine, wellearned "curiosity ," not an unr easonable demand.
3. How Checking Actually Works: Cr oss-V erification and the "Bus Stand" Analogy

1. Bhaiya explains that he personally cr oss-verifies and trains every mentor , clearing their doubts dir ectly — so even sangat members whose aura checking wasn't done by Bhaiya's own dir ect attention have still had it filter ed through his oversight of the mentor system. 2. A telephone-game-style analogy is offer ed: if the same message ("I am standing her e at the bus stand") is r elayed through Baba to Bhaiya and separately to a mentor , one might r etain only "I am standing her e" and the other only "at the bus stand" — the two halves must be combined by mutual coordination to r econstruct the full, accurate message. 3. The stated lesson: this is pr ecisely why coordination and cooperation between mentors, Bhaiya, and the sangat is essential — and why even a practitioner whose drishti has alr eady opened still needs continued coordination with the wider Ashaeiynn structur e rather than r elying solely on their own per ception.
4. No One Is "Complete" — Continuous Learning Even After Attainment

1. Bhaiya states plainly that no one is "purna" (fully complete) — anyone who claims otherwise is not — and that the mor e knowledge his own guru continues to r eveal to him, the mor e he personally r ealizes how much he still doesn't know . 2. He recalls that early on, when his guru began teaching him various vidyas, some newcomers to the sangat likely found his explanations confusing — he r eassur es such newcomers that clarity will come with time and dir ect conversation.
5. The First Visions: Recurring Dr eams During College

1. Bhaiya shar es that during his third year of college (having completed his graduation in Chemistry Honours befor e eventually pursuing further studies), he began experiencing r ecurring dr eams and visions of Hanuman Ji Maharaj in a meditative postur e — which he initially ignor ed and told no one about, having been mocked once alr eady after mentioning it to hostel friends.
6. The Defining Night: A Full-Moon Vision on the Wall

1. On a specific night he r ecalls pr ecisely (ar ound 3:00–3:10 a.m., which he identifies as a full-moon night), Bhaiya describes feeling his chest pr essed, waking with a start, and — thr ough moonlight str eaming thr ough his window and forming what he describes as a natural "scr een" on the opposite wall — seeing a dir ect manifestation of Hanuman Ji Maharaj, accompanied by an inner voice/r ealization: "This is your guru." 2. He describes being overwhelmed for roughly 10–15 minutes afterward — goosebumps, tr embling, and a loss of ordinary awar eness — noting that similar , lesser signs had occurr ed once or twice befor e, which he had pr eviously dismissed, but this particular incident was differ ent in intensity and impact.
7. Scientific Skepticism and the Sear ch for a "Logical" Path

1. Despite the vision's impact, Bhaiya states he r emained r esistant to accepting it outright, attributing this to his science backgr ound (Chemistry) and his instinct to demand logical gr ounding for any claim. 2. He describes deliberately r ejecting the many "quick-r esult" mantra rituals he found online (e.g., "see Hanuman Ji in 40 days," "in 10 days") as inauthentic shortcuts, r easoning that if Hanuman Ji Maharaj wer e real, his connection to Him could not be r educed to a scripted internet ritual.
8. The Origin of "Jai Siyaram" as His Personal Mantra

1. Seeking guidance, Bhaiya appr oached an elder relative (his "badi dadi"), who told him simply to look at what Hanuman Ji Maharaj himself does in the Ramayana — that he chants "Jai Siyaram" — and to do the same. 2. Bhaiya describes an immediate, intense bodily r eaction (goosebumps fr om head to toe) upon hearing this suggestion, which he took as confirmation that this was the specific practice meant for him — and states that fr om that day onward, this became his committed mantra.
9. Escalating Practice and Its Toll

1. For the first one and a half years of chanting "Jai Siyaram," Bhaiya states he r eceived no per ceptible result whatsoever , despite steadily incr easing his daily practice fr om one hour up to ten hours a day over time. 2. He describes sever e physical decline (extr eme thinness, a visibly wasted body) and his par ents' shifting r eactions — from anger , to pity , to eventually grudging acknowledgment of his sheer persistence — while he continued to tell them only that he intended to keep chanting "Jai Siyaram."
10. Three Years of Watching Others Succeed While He Did Not

1. This teaching states that over roughly thr ee years, everyone Bhaiya personally taught the mantra to went on to have their own drishti open and r eceive dir ect darshan of Hanuman Ji Maharaj — while he himself r eceived nothing, leading to an extended period of self-blame and despair , including believing he must have accumulated extr emely sever e past karma to be denied while everyone he helped succeeded.
1 1. The Pandit's Kundli Reading and the "Guru Sthan Mangal" Turning Point

1. Concerned r elatives arranged for a pandit to examine his birth chart, who identified kaal sarp dosh, an afflicted Mars, a weak Surya, and a weak Brihaspati (Jupiter) — pr edicting a life of struggle (debt, hardship, difficulty) but confirming basic survival ("guzara ho jayega"). 2. Bhaiya then posed a hypothetical question to the pandit: what would it mean if Mars wer e positioned specifically in a person's "guru sthan" (the house governing one's guru/teacher) in their birth chart? The pandit's answer — "raj yog" (a auspicious, kingly combination) — became the decisive personal confirmation Bhaiya needed that his path with Hanuman Ji as guru was destined to succeed, r egardless of how difficult it curr ently felt.
12. Continued Testing, Doubt, and the Sankat Mochan Hanuman Ashtak

1. Bhaiya describes his guru r epeatedly undermining his gr owing confidence just as it built — including one specific incident where he found himself unable to even perform his r egular puja, leading to a moment of complete despair (crying in fr ont of the temple, feeling that even his one r emaining devotional outlet was being taken fr om him). 2. In this moment of crisis, he r ecited the Sankat Mochan Hanuman Ashtak, specifically invoking the verse r eferencing Hanuman Ji devouring the sun as an infant (bal samay ravi bhaksh liyo) — and states that this specific r ecitation marked a turning point, after which that same night's jaap session br ought a r enewed resolve never to abandon Ram's name r egardless of outcome.
13. The Ankur Relationship: Watching Through Another's Drishti

1. A pivotal figur e in this narrative is Ankur, someone Bhaiya personally gave the mantra to, whose own drishti opened within 90 days — while Bhaiya's own drishti still had not opened after roughly five years of intensive practice. 2. Despite possessing far gr eater accumulated mantra shakti fr om his years of practice, Bhaiya describes himself in this period as effectively "blind," r elying on Ankur (whose drishti was open) to narrate what he was per ceiving in various lokas — comparing this to a blind man being guided by a walking stick.
14. The Loka Journey: Weeping Without Seeing

1. In one especially emotional episode, the two of them "traveled" together (in meditation, at night, with the r oom lights off to avoid alerting Bhaiya's par ents) to Hanuman Ji Maharaj's loka — Ankur could see Hanuman Ji dir ectly and reported this to Bhaiya, who wept out of longing despite seeing nothing himself, praying aloud that he had come to his guru's own r ealm yet still could not behold him dir ectly . 2. Ankur then told Bhaiya something that devastated him further — that he could actually see tears falling fr om Bhaiya's own subtle body (sookshma sharir), even though Bhaiya's physical eyes could per ceive nothing at all — a moment Bhaiya describes as deeply painful, since Ankur could witness this intimate pr oof of his devotion while he himself remained unable to see anything.
15. The Crocodile-Faced Attacker Revealed as an Embrace

1. Later in that same episode, something with a cr ocodile-like face struck Bhaiya's subtle body dir ectly , causing him r eal pain — which Ankur then reinterpreted for him: what had struck him was in fact a large, gorilla-like manifestation of Hanuman Ji Maharaj himself, and what felt like an attack was actually Hanuman Ji embracing him.

2. This reframing br ought Bhaiya to tears of a differ ent kind — relief and gratitude — leading him to declar e that he no longer needed that kind of dir ect visual "drishti" at all; simply being embraced by his guru, even without the ability to see it happen, was enough for him to dedicate his entir e life to that name r egardless of whether he ever gained sight of it.
16. Developing Remote Per ception — Verified Externally

1. Following this turning point, Bhaiya describes gradually being able to per ceive and accurately describe other people's household deities, spatial layouts, and specific cir cumstances at a distance — initially tested skeptically by Ankur (asking about his own maternal r elative's home shrine, which Bhaiya described corr ectly down to specific idol placement) and later independently verified by his friend Vinay and Vinay's father , including describing an exact r oom layout and specific ritual details he had never seen in person.
17. Tantrik Encounters and Dir ect Vidya Instruction fr om Hanuman Ji

1. Bhaiya describes his guru pr ogr essively intr oducing him to a wide range of tantriks of varying power — including one capable of r emotely "counting his br eaths" to spy on him — with each new challenge met by his guru teaching him a fresh countermeasur e or vidya exactly when the pr evious appr oach stopped working, describing this pr ocess as being deliberately "forged like in a furnace." 2. He states that all of his tantra-mantra-yantra knowledge, aura-r eading ability , and ritual practice (including r eceiving formal "guru diksha" and a specific guru mantra) came dir ectly fr om Hanuman Ji Maharaj as his guru — explicitly rejecting the assumption that guru diksha can only be given by a human guru.
18. The "Water" Analogy: One Tattva, Countless Applications

1. Bhaiya offers an illustrative analogy: the same water , pour ed into differ ent vessels, takes differ ent shapes — similarly , a single mantra or tattva can be applied thr ough countless differ ent specific vidyas (to nourish, to harm, to purify , to cut, and so on) depending on the specific technique taught — but access to these specific applications is only possible through a guru, never through self-teaching alone.
19. The "Dimension" Concept: Why His Own Journey Took Five Years

1. This teaching's key structural concept: each person carries a specific spiritual "dimension" (a level of accumulated tapasya/attainment) fr om their past lives, and in this life a practitioner must first re-reach that exact past-life dimension befor e gaining access to the corr esponding siddhis and abilities — illustrated with specific hypothetical benchmark figur es (e.g., a person whose past-life dimension stopped at "5,000" will r each it quickly in this life, while someone whose past-life dimension r eached "10 lakh cr or e" will require corr espondingly much mor e tapasya to cr oss that same threshold again). 2. Bhaiya states his own past-life dimension was extr emely high, which is why his own journey specifically r equired roughly five years of intensive effort — but adds that once such a high thr eshold is cr ossed, that person becomes essentially impossible for lower -level negativity or manipulation to confuse or disturb, since only entities above that same dimension could have any effect on them at all.
20. Reassurance: "Y ou Are All Chosen," and Negativity Is Universal

1. Bhaiya states dir ectly , invoking Hanuman Ji Maharaj as witness, that everyone pr esent in the sangat is specifically "chosen" — not random attendees — and that their prior connection to Ashaeiynn and to him is a genuine, earned one, not a coincidence. 2. He states that negativity or pitru-related pr oblems affecting nearly everyone is not itself unusual or alarming — with a rough population illustrating how widespr ead unr esolved deaths/spirits necessarily ar e — the crucial differ ence is realizing one's own negativity exists and beginning consistent jaap in r esponse, since even jaap begun pur ely to r emove
negativity gradually grants r eal bhakti and elevates a person back toward their own past-life dimension r egardless of the original motive.
21. What Happens Once a Person Reaches Their Past-Life Dimension

1. This teaching states that once someone cr osses back into their own past-life dimension, they gain sudden clarity about their life's actual purpose and motivation, along with access to accumulated siddhis and energies fr om potentially hundreds or thousands of past-life efforts — becoming, in effect, no longer "a single person," and unstoppable in that specific ar ea of work. 2. A closing r eassurance offer ed specifically to the sangat: no one at Ashaeiynn will need anywher e near as long as Bhaiya himself did — roughly 75% of practitioners can expect some per ceptible experience on their very first dedicated attempt, with darshan pr omised to all within four sittings, pr ovided sincer e intention (bhaav) is maintained.
22. Practical Guidance and Session Logistics

1. Bhaiya offers a specific practical suggestion for anyone wanting Baba's darshan during the upcoming Sunday mantrachanting meeting: light a diya, keep an image of Prabhu nearby if possible, clear the room, verbally ask any negativity to leave, and then begin one's own name-mantra jaap while the meeting plays. 2. The session closes with an announcement of an upcoming Purnima Maha Yagya, confirmation that a Google form will follow shortly after the meeting ends, and that the next meeting will begin the following day at 12:30.
QUICK RULES SUMMARY

The sangat's collective jaap is pr oducing rapid drishti-openings at an unpr ecedented rate , tracked via weekly video updates for those unable to attend live. The constant demand for mantra/aura checking is understandable, not excessive — physical-world ef fort rarely shows visible results, so people naturally seek reassurance in the subtle world instead; all mentor -performed checks are personally cross-verified and trained by Bhaiya. No one, including Bhaiya himself, is ever fully "complete" — continued coordination with the wider Ashaeiynn structure remains necessary even after drishti opens, illustrated via the "bus stand" telephone-game analogy . Bhaiya's own path began with r ecurring dr eam visions of Hanuman Ji Maharaj in college, culminating in a specific fullmoon-night dir ect wall vision identifying Hanuman Ji as his guru. His specific mantra, "Jai Siyaram," was chosen on the guidance of an elder relative (pointing to what Hanuman Ji himself chants in the Ramayana), confirmed for him by an immediate, intense bodily reaction. He practiced for five years without his own drishti opening, even as everyone he personally taught the mantra to received their own darshan — a period marked by severe physical toll, family friction, a pandit's kundli reading (including the pivotal "Mars in guru sthan = raj yog" hypothetical), and deep personal despair . His companion Ankur's drishti opened within 90 days of r eceiving the mantra, leading to an extended period wher e Bhaiya r elied entirely on Ankur's sight — including a pivotal loka-journey episode where Ankur alone could see Hanuman Ji and Bhaiya's own weeping subtle body , and where what felt like a painful attack was revealed to be Hanuman Ji's own embrace. After this, Bhaiya explicitly chose devotion and connection over the need for literal visual "drishti" itself — and later developed verified remote-perception abilities, confirmed independently through friends' testing. All of Bhaiya's tantra-mantra-yantra knowledge and formal guru diksha came dir ectly fr om Hanuman Ji Maharaj as guru, with no human guru involved at any point. The cor e structural concept intr oduced in this session: each person carries a specific past-life spiritual "dimension" that must be re-reached befor e corr esponding siddhis become accessible — Bhaiya's own unusually high past-life dimension is why his personal journey took five years, while most practitioners' thresholds are far lower and faster to reach.

Every sangat member is described as specifically "chosen," and near -universal negativity/pitru pr oblems ar e not unusual — the key dif ferentiator is recognizing one's own negativity and beginning consistent jaap, which gradually grants real bhakti regardless of initial motive. Spelling note: the institute's name is written "Ashaeiynn" — use this spelling consistently .
Part II — Q&A Pairs (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Q&A Pairs (Session 46, English)
Bhaiya's Guru Journey: The Night of Vision, the Origin of "Jai Siyaram," and the Dimension of Past-Life Tapasya
User-style questions with answers gr ounded in this Ashaeiynn live session. Gr eeting style: "Jai Siya Ram."

Q1. Is the sangat's collective mantra jaap actually pr oducing r esults? A: Yes — per this teaching, Bhaiya states the collective jaap performed on the sangat's behalf is bearing fruit at an unprecedented, unlimited level, with devotees receiving darshan in rapid succession and weekly video updates documenting this ongoing pattern.

Q2. Why do sangat members ask for mantra/aura checking so often? A: Per this teaching, Bhaiya explains this is understandable rather than excessive: in the physical world, ef fort rarely shows visible results, so people naturally seek reassurance in the subtle world instead — wanting confirmation that negativity is clearing and Ram's ener gy is taking its place.

Q3. Does Bhaiya personally check every single person's aura himself? A: Not always directly — but this teaching states he personally cross-verifies and trains every mentor , clearing their doubts directly , so even checks performed by mentors are filtered through his oversight.

Q4. Why does it matter that mentors and Bhaiya coordinate on what they each per ceive? A: This teaching uses a telephone-gamestyle analogy — "I am standing here at the bus stand" — where one listener retains only "I am standing here" and another only "at the bus stand"; the full, accurate picture only emer ges when both pieces are combined through coordination.

Q5. Once someone's drishti opens, do they still need to coordinate with Ashaeiynn's structur e? A: Yes — per this teaching, no one is ever "purna" (fully complete), and continued coordination with mentors and Bhaiya remains necessary even after drishti opens, rather than relying solely on one's own perception.

Q6. When did Bhaiya first start experiencing visions of Hanuman Ji Maharaj? A: During his third year of college, after completing his graduation in Chemistry Honours — he began having recurring dreams of Hanuman Ji Maharaj in a meditative posture, which he initially ignored and told no one about after being mocked once.

Q7. What happened on the specific night Bhaiya describes as the turning point? A: On a full-moon night around 3:00–3:10 a.m., he felt his chest pressed and woke with a start; moonlight through his window created a natural "screen" ef fect on the opposite wall, where he directly perceived Hanuman Ji Maharaj's form, accompanied by an inner realization: "This is your guru."

Q8. Did Bhaiya immediately accept this vision as r eal? A: Not entirely — per this teaching, his science background (Chemistry) made him instinctively skeptical and eager for logical grounding, leading him to reject the many "quick-result" online mantra rituals he encountered (such as claims of seeing Hanuman Ji within 40 or 10 days) as inauthentic shortcuts.

Q9. How did Bhaiya settle on "Jai Siyaram" as his personal mantra? A: An elder relative (his "badi dadi") told him to simply look at what Hanuman Ji Maharaj himself does in the Ramayana — chant "Jai Siyaram" — and do the same; Bhaiya describes an immediate, intense bodily reaction confirming this was the right practice for him.

Q10. Did Bhaiya see r esults quickly after starting this practice? A: No — per this teaching, he received no perceptible result for the first one and a half years, despite steadily increasing his daily practice from one hour up to ten hours a day .

Q1 1. How did this level of practice affect Bhaiya physically and with his family? A: He describes severe physical decline (extreme thinness) and his parents' reactions shifting from anger , to pity , to eventual grudging acknowledgment of his persistence, while he continued to tell them only that he intended to keep chanting.

Q12. Did everyone Bhaiya taught the mantra to eventually get r esults? A: Yes — per this teaching, over roughly three years, everyone he personally taught the mantra to went on to have their own drishti open and receive direct darshan, while he himself received nothing, leading to an extended period of self-blame and despair .

Q13. What did a pandit's r eading of Bhaiya's birth chart r eveal? A: Kaal sarp dosh, an af flicted Mars, a weak Surya, and a weak Brihaspati — predicting a life of struggle and hardship, though confirming basic survival.

Q14. What was the "guru sthan mangal" moment, and why did it matter so much to Bhaiya? A: Bhaiya asked the pandit hypothetically what it would mean if Mars were positioned in a person's "guru sthan" (the house governing one's guru); the pandit's answer — "raj yog" (an auspicious combination) — became Bhaiya's decisive personal confirmation that his path with Hanuman Ji as guru was destined to succeed despite the dif ficulty .

Q15. Did Bhaiya's confidence ever waver again after this? A: Yes — this teaching describes his guru repeatedly undermining his growing confidence, including one incident where he found himself unable to even perform his regular puja, leading to complete despair .

Q16. What br ought Bhaiya thr ough that specific crisis? A: He recited the Sankat Mochan Hanuman Ashtak, specifically invoking the verse about Hanuman Ji devouring the sun as an infant — this teaching states this recitation marked a turning point, followed that same night by renewed resolve never to abandon Ram's name regardless of outcome.

Q17. Who is Ankur, and why is he significant in this story? A: Ankur was someone Bhaiya personally gave the mantra to, whose own drishti opened within just 90 days — while Bhaiya's own drishti still had not opened after roughly five years of far more intensive practice.

Q18. How did Bhaiya describe his own position during this period, r elative to Ankur? A: Despite possessing far greater accumulated mantra shakti, he describes himself as ef fectively "blind," relying on Ankur to narrate what he perceived — comparing himself to a blind man being guided by a walking stick.

Q19. What happened during the pivotal "loka journey" episode with Ankur? A: The two traveled together in meditation to Hanuman Ji Maharaj's loka; Ankur could see Hanuman Ji directly and reported this, while Bhaiya wept out of longing despite perceiving nothing himself — and Ankur then revealed he could see tears falling from Bhaiya's own subtle body , even though Bhaiya's physical eyes saw nothing at all.

Q20. What was the cr ocodile-faced attacker that struck Bhaiya during this episode? A: Something with a crocodile-like face struck his subtle body , causing real pain — which Ankur then reinterpreted as a lar ge, gorilla-like manifestation of Hanuman Ji Maharaj embracing him, meaning what felt like an attack was actually a divine embrace.

Q21. How did Bhaiya r eact once he understood this r eframing? A: With tears of relief and gratitude — he declared he no longer needed literal visual "drishti" at all; simply being embraced by his guru, even without seeing it happen, was enough to dedicate his entire life to that name regardless of whether sight ever came.

Q22. Did Bhaiya eventually develop his own per ceptive abilities? A: Yes — he describes gradually being able to accurately perceive and describe others' household deities and specific circumstances at a distance, tested skeptically by Ankur and later independently verified by his friend Vinay and Vinay's father , including exact room layouts and ritual details he had never seen in person.

Q23. Did Bhaiya have a human guru who taught him tantra-mantra-yantra techniques? A: No — per this teaching, all of his tantra-mantra-yantra knowledge, aura-reading ability , formal guru diksha, and guru mantra came directly from Hanuman Ji Maharaj as his guru, with no human guru involved at any point.

Q24. What does the "water" analogy in this session illustrate? A: That the same water , poured into dif ferent vessels, takes dif ferent shapes — similarly , a single mantra or tattva can be applied through countless dif ferent specific vidyas depending on the technique taught, but access to these specific applications is only possible through a guru, never through self-teaching.

Q25. What is the "dimension" concept intr oduced in this session? A: Each person carries a specific spiritual "dimension" (a level of accumulated tapasya) from their past lives, and in this life a practitioner must first re-reach that exact past-life dimension before gaining access to the corresponding siddhis — someone whose past-life dimension was low reaches it quickly , while someone whose past-life dimension was very high (like Bhaiya's own) requires correspondingly much more tapasya.

Q26. Why did Bhaiya's own journey specifically take five years? A: Per this teaching, his own past-life dimension was extremely high, requiring roughly five years of intensive ef fort to re-reach — though once such a high threshold is crossed, a person becomes essentially impossible for lower -level negativity or manipulation to disturb.

Q27. Does Bhaiya consider the sangat members' pr esence at Ashaeiynn to be coincidental? A: No — he states directly , invoking Hanuman Ji Maharaj as witness, that everyone present is specifically "chosen," and their connection to Ashaeiynn and to him is genuine and earned, not random.

Q28. Is having negativity or pitru-related pr oblems unusual? A: No — this teaching states it af fects nearly everyone and is not itself alarming; the crucial dif ference is recognizing one's own negativity and beginning consistent jaap in response, which gradually grants real bhakti regardless of the original motive.

Q29. What happens once someone r eaches their own past-life dimension? A: This teaching states they gain sudden clarity about their life's actual purpose, along with access to accumulated siddhis and ener gies from potentially hundreds or thousands of past-life efforts, becoming ef fectively unstoppable in that specific area of work.

Q30. Will other sangat members need as long as Bhaiya did to see r esults? A: No — this teaching of fers a direct reassurance that no one at Ashaeiynn will need anywhere near five years; roughly 75% of practitioners can expect some perceptible experience on their very first dedicated attempt, with darshan promised to all within four sittings, provided sincere intention is maintained.

Q31. What practical steps does Bhaiya suggest for someone wanting Baba's darshan during a mantra-chanting meeting? A: Light a diya, keep an image of Prabhu nearby if possible, clear the room, verbally ask any negativity to leave, and then begin one's own name-mantra jaap while the meeting plays.
Bot Response Guidelines (Session 46 additions)

Present Bhaiya's specific vision-night account (the moonlit "screen" on the wall, the chest-pressing sensation) as his own personal, biographical testimony — not as a universal or expected experience for practitioners. Preserve the specific origin story of "Jai Siyaram" (guided by an elder relative's reference to Hanuman Ji's own practice in the Ramayana) accurately , and keep it distinct from generic mantra-selection advice — this was Bhaiya's own personal confirmation process, not a required ritual for others. Keep the pandit/kundli episode (kaal sarp dosh, the "Mars in guru sthan = raj yog" hypothetical) framed as Bhaiya's own biographical detail and personal source of reassurance, not as astrological guidance to be generalized to other practitioners' charts. Handle the Ankur "loka journey" narrative (weeping without seeing, the crocodile-faced attacker revealed as an embrace) with care and accuracy — this is one of the most emotionally significant episodes in Bhaiya's account and should not be summarized

in a way that flattens its emotional arc (initial pain and confusion, resolved into relief and devotion). Present the "dimension" concept (past-life spiritual level that must be re-reached) consistently with prior sessions' related concepts (Maha Sookshma Sharir , accumulated past-life siddhis) — this session's specific numeric illustrations (e.g., "5,000" vs. "10 lakh crore") are Bhaiya's own hypothetical teaching figures, not literally verified statistics. When reassuring practitioners about timelines, preserve the specific figures given (roughly 75% experiencing something on the first attempt, darshan promised within four sittings) as this teaching's own stated expectations, while noting that individual experiences may vary . Present the "you are all chosen" statement and the "negativity is universal" reassurance together , since this teaching frames them as directly related: recognizing one's own negativity and beginning jaap is what activates a person's chosen path, not a sign of being spiritually behind. Spelling note: the institute's name is written "Ashaeiynn" — use this spelling consistently .

Bhaiya's Teachings — Curated Conversational Supplement (Session 46, Hinglish)
Bhaiya ki Apni Guru-Yatra: Live Sangat Reactions

Yeh Part III har session mein nahi hota — sirf tab jab sour ce transcript mein genuine live sangat conversation ho.
